response: Amblyopia, also known as lazy eye, is a condition that can cause visual loss. However, the visual loss associated with amblyopia is not always permanent. In some cases, older people with a history of amblyopia who develop visual loss in the previously normal eye can experience recovery of visual function in the amblyopic eye over a period of time. This recovery in visual function occurs in the wake of visual loss in the fellow eye and the improvement appears to be sustained. Nevertheless, it's essential to note that the effectiveness of recovery may vary depending on individual circumstances, and treatment of amblyopia may not always result in complete normalization of visual function.
